newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan TAIEX stocks drop 1.99 pct as OTC tumbles.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan TAIEX stocks drop 1.99 pct as OTC tumbles.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Wednesday, dragged down by profit-taking against big recent gains in electronics and a sharp downturn in the fledgling over-the-counter exchange, brokers said. The main TAIEX index ended down 156.87 points or 1.99 percent at 7,730.49, off an opening high of 7,950.99.
Turnover was a very hectic T$179.27 billion, the highest in more than three years.
Wednesday's turnover exceeded the sizzling T$166.9 billion notched on Friday and marked the highest total since T$185.9 billion in stock changed hands on January 6, 1994.
The OTC stock index tumbled 4.03 percent to close at 260.26 points, with securities brokerage shares leading the fall.
Brokers attributed the OTC fall and, in turn, the TAIEX's, to the Securities and Exchange Commission's rejection on Tuesday of Capital Securities' planned T$800 million OTC rights issue.
"Investors speculate that the rejection...indicates the government is trying to cool down both stock markets' recent bull runs," said Eric Liu of National Securities.
Brokers said the downturn also reflected heavy profit-taking on recent bellwether shares, especially electronics.

Electronics plunged 4.17 percent due to Tuesday's official word that export orders for electronics products fell an annual 9.69 percent in January while those for telecommunications and information products fell a year-on-year 5.36 percent.
"As expected, electronics' first-quarter sales performance will not be good. The sector should continue to consolidate," said National Securities analyst Oliver Fang.
Acer computer fell T$1.5 to T$58. Microelectronics plunged the daily seven percent limit to T$44.3.
